_provenance.local_operation: C_GenerateKeyPair(CKM_ML_KEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN) with CKA_SEED = d || z (64 bytes) in the PRIVATE-key template; the generated public key CKA_VALUE is byte-compared to ek and the private key CKA_VALUE (generated non-sensitive, extractable) to dk
_provenance.transformation: subset only; tcId, d, z, ek, dk byte-copied from the upstream file (hex case preserved); no value is re-derived
_provenance.subset_policy: Deterministic. Three cases per parameter-set group: the lowest tcId, the tcId at sorted position floor(n/2), and the highest tcId (the keyGen groups have no further properties to span).
_provenance.retained_fields: tcId, d, z, ek, dk (deferred dropped)
_provenance.interface_note: PKCS#11 v3.2 section 6.68 lists CKA_SEED among the attributes the key-pair mechanism contributes; accepting a caller-supplied seed is engine behaviour, not a specification requirement. The C++ engine rejects CKA_SEED in the public-key template (CKR_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_INVALID); both engines accept it in the private-key template, which is the one used here.
_provenance.test_only_key_material: d, z and dk are public NIST ACVP-Server sample data; generated objects are session objects (CKA_TOKEN=false) destroyed after the case
